equatorialToPolarRadius.cell: 1.089 ± 0.017 (abstract: the equatorial radius is 1.089 times the polar radius)

poleTemperatureK.cell: 10170 ± 450 (Table 1 and section 3.2: Gaudi et al. 2017's effective temperature taken as the polar temperature)

oblateness.note: As 1 - R_pole/R_eq this is a ratio of 1.098; the abstract states 1.089. The abstract's ratio is used.

equatorPoleContrast.cell: 'its local surface brightness to vary by ~38% between its hot poles and cooler equator' (abstract); 'varies in effective temperature by ~800 K' (Figure 2 caption); 'nearly 1000 K' (section 2)

note: The paper fits its own gravity-darkening model (Ahlers et al. 2016: surface gravity to second order with a centrifugal term; oblateness from the Darwin-Radau relation) and does not publish ω or an equatorial temperature. Here the Roche-von Zeipel model of the other rapid rotators takes the paper's radius ratio and β: its ω is the Roche surface with that ratio, and the equator comes out about 500 K cooler than the pole, less than the 800 to 1000 K the paper's text states (tools/objects/observation/gravity-darkening.test.mts).
